name: Init Ding
editorial_article:
"Init Ding" is the seminal 1995 debut album by Microstoria, the collaborative project between electronic musicians Markus Popp (best known for his work as Oval) and Jan St. Werner (co-founder of Mouse on Mars). Released on the Thrill Jockey label, the album stands as a cornerstone of the 1990s experimental electronic landscape, specifically in the development of "glitch" and ambient music. By deconstructing and reassembling digital fragments, Microstoria forged a sonic identity that was both fragile and deeply intricate, often described by listeners as "the sound of computers dreaming."

The album marked a departure from more conventional techno or ambient structures, favoring microscopic sound design and non-linear patterns that challenged listeners to engage with digital artifacts as melodic and rhythmic building blocks. The influence of "Init Ding" is profound, having set a blueprint for subsequent generations of IDM and experimental artists who sought to treat digital errors as textures. Decades later, the work remains remarkably fresh, with its reissues—often coupled with the project's equally heralded work "_snd"—continuing to be cited in critical surveys of essential ambient music. Its legacy is one of technical curiosity meeting emotional depth, proving that the rigid architecture of early digital sound could be bent into fluid, evocative shapes.
editorial_pitch: A foundational 1995 glitch-ambient milestone by Microstoria (Markus Popp & Jan St. Werner) that transformed digital artifacts into the architecture of modern experimental electronic music.
